Home needs accessibility service access to perform this gesture action (lock screen, recent apps, quick settings, or power dialog).

This service only performs the system action you assigned. It does not read screen content, collect personal data, or transmit any information. All processing stays on your device.

You will be taken to accessibility settings to enable Home actions.
Home needs notification access to show your notifications here. You will be taken to Android settings to grant this permission.
Home needs to be the default home screen to access private space.

Home wallpaper is a "faux" wallpaper, it's an image that appears over the actual android wallpaper layer.

It's function it's meant to circumvent Android cropping and zooming in your wallpaper which might break the the 1:1 pixel scaling which can cause defect to your image especially if you're using an e-ink device.

Make sure to use correct aspect ratio, or have the exact resolution as your display.

Setting an Android wallpaper will automatically clear the Home wallpaper.
Home does not track you. It does not collect, store, or share your data.

Home has no server of its own. It uses the network for one thing: when you open Ecosystem apps or ask for an app there, it reaches GitHub to see the latest version and to download it. Nothing about you or your phone is sent.
Home only previews and displays data that already exists on your phone. All app information, notifications, and settings are processed locally and stay on your device.
Home is open source. You can review the source code on GitHub to verify these claims.

Home uses this accessibility service for two things: to perform the system actions you assign to gestures (lock screen, open recent apps, open quick settings, open the power dialog), and to show music controls on the lock screen for players other than Mudita\'s own. For the second it watches only the system lock screen, to know when it is showing and whether the PIN pad is up. It does not read other apps, and it does not collect, store or share anything. No data leaves your device.

Home is a plain, quiet home screen, a fork of inkOS by gezimos. It is the front door to a family of apps that work together: a press on the clock opens Time, a contact opens Connections, and the home screen carries a few lines from the others.
Home does not collect, store, or share any data, and there is no tracking. The only connection it makes is to GitHub, when you get or update your apps.
To continue, agree to the privacy policy
Let Home read your notifications, so it can show them on the home screen.
Make Home the screen your phone opens to. You can change this later.
Settings: pinch on an empty part of the home screen. Quick settings open, and All Settings is there.
Tick the box to say you have read where Settings is
Choose a color preset, or keep the look you have.
Pick the apps for your home screen and put them in order. The apps you just got are in the list.
Allow Home to install apps on the screen that opened, come back, and press GET again.

This app is made by wander wildwood, an independent developer: one person, not a company. That makes wander wildwood the data controller for anything the app itself handles, and that is very little: your layout and settings stay on this phone unless you send a backup somewhere yourself, and nothing comes to the developer.
Write to email@wanderthe.dev, about your data or anything else.

Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to limit or object to its use, to take a copy with you, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a data protection authority. Since the app keeps what it stores only on your phone, you can do most of this yourself: clear the app\'s data in Android\'s settings, or uninstall the app. What GitHub receives when you get or update an app is covered by its own privacy policy.
